response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-21
CLINICAL INDICATION: Emergency department. Shortness of breath. History of prostate cancer on hormone therapy. Portable film.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. J. Marte (synthetic), ED
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-06-30. Note: the prior report says heart size normal, but both blind reads saw an enlarged cardiac silhouette on the prior PA image. The prior report does not mention the left pectoral cardiac device that is visible on the prior image. It says lungs clear, which mostly agrees, though one read noted mildly prominent right perihilar markings and a slightly hazy left costophrenic angle on the prior. The prior report may be incomplete or may not belong to this image, and this should be verified.
TECHNIQUE: Current film is AP, labeled supine, portable, with low inspiration and mild rotation. Prior film is PA, appears upright, with adequate inspiration and mild rotation. Projection and position differ from the prior. Comparison is limited.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F1: Tubular density over the trachea consistent with an endotracheal tube, tip over the upper thoracic trachea, carina not clearly defined, tip-to-carina relationship unconfirmed. Reads disagreed on status. Triage: critical, page on-call flagged. The indication does not mention intubation.
- F3: Increased coarse reticular and hazy opacity, right mid zone.
- F4: Increased coarse reticular and hazy opacity, left mid zone.
- F5: Hazy opacity, right lower zone, indeterminate.
- F6: Hazy opacity, left base and retrocardiac region, indeterminate.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is roughly midline allowing for rotation. A tubular density projects over the tracheal air column, consistent with an endotracheal tube, with its tip over the upper thoracic trachea. The carina is not clearly seen. This tube is not present on the prior. INDETERMINATE (F1): the two blind reads disagreed on status (read A: new, read B: stable). The merge note in the data suggests this may be a pairing artifact, with both reads calling the tube new. Resident to verify. Lung volumes are low. Bilateral coarse reticular and hazy opacities are present in the perihilar, mid and lower zones. Right mid zone (F3) and left mid zone (F4) markings are denser and less sharp than on the prior, increased on both reads, with supine AP technique contributing to part of the appearance. Hazy opacity at the right lower zone with indistinct right hemidiaphragm margin (F5) and at the left base and retrocardiac region with poorly defined left hemidiaphragm (F6) is INDETERMINATE (both reads indeterminate). Atelectasis, airspace opacity and layering pleural fluid are all possible, and low volumes and supine position can mimic basal opacity. No focal mass is seen within the limits of the film. Prior: well inflated lungs, mild prominence of right perihilar and lower zone markings, no confluent consolidation, no discrete nodule or mass.
- Mediastinum / hila: Upper mediastinum looks broader on this AP supine film than on the prior PA, but width is not reliable (F8). INDETERMINATE: only one read recorded this finding, as indeterminate. Hila are indistinct with perihilar haze, more evident on the right. Rotation differs between films.
- Pleura: No pleural line is seen, but a supine film is insensitive for pneumothorax. Hazy increased density over both lower zones with indistinct costophrenic regions; layering effusions cannot be excluded. Both domes are high, consistent with low inspiration and supine position, and the left dome is poorly defined behind the heart. No free gas is seen, though a supine film is insensitive for this. Prior: no pneumothorax, right costophrenic angle clear, left costophrenic angle partly obscured by the enlarged heart, no large effusion.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged on both films (F7). Interval change in size cannot be judged because the current film is AP supine with low inspiration, which magnifies the heart. Left heart border is partly indistinct on the current film. Left pectoral cardiac device with multiple transvenous leads, including shock coils over the superior vena cava region and the right ventricle region, is present on both films. No lead discontinuity is seen at this resolution. The right ventricular coil projects lower on the current film, which is expected from the change in projection, position and inspiration. INDETERMINATE (F2): the two blind reads disagreed on status (read A: stable, read B: new). The merge note suggests a pairing artifact, with both reads calling the cardiac device stable. Resident to verify.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib or clavicle fracture is seen, though fine bone detail is limited on the portable film. No definite destructive bone lesion is seen at this resolution. No soft tissue gas. ECG electrodes and external lines overlie the chest. A looped density over the lower midline may be an enteric tube or external hardware.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Tubular density consistent with an endotracheal tube, not on the prior (F1, reads disagreed, indeterminate). Increased hazy and reticular opacity in the right and left mid zones (F3, F4), with technique contributing. Basal hazy opacities (F5, F6) are denser or less defined than on the prior but indeterminate because of low volumes and supine position.
- Unchanged: Left pectoral cardiac device with the same lead configuration on both films (F2, reads disagreed, indeterminate). Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both films, but size change cannot be judged (F7). Apparent upper mediastinal widening is not comparable across projections (F8, indeterminate). No size change is reported for any focal finding.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs. No confirmed measurements.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the heart size changed? (Reads A and B) | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP supine portable with low inspiration. Magnification differs between the two. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or echocardiography or CT chest if clinically needed.
- Are pleural effusions present, and are they new? (Read A) | Reason: On a supine film fluid layers posteriorly and appears as hazy density rather than a meniscus. Both bases are hazy, with low volumes also contributing. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is there a left pleural effusion or left lower zone collapse behind the heart? (Read A) | Reason: Retrocardiac density on a single frontal supine film, with an enlarged heart and a poorly defined left hemidiaphragm. | Recommend: Lateral view when the patient is able, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is the basal opacity true consolidation or atelectasis from low volumes? (Read A) | Reason: Current film is supine with low lung volumes, which crowds the lower zones and mimics basal opacity. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration when possible, or CT chest.
- Is the endotracheal tube tip at a satisfactory level above the carina, and is an enteric tube present? (Read A) | Reason: The carina is not clearly defined on this compressed image. Multiple external lines and a looped density over the lower midline overlap the mediastinum and upper abdomen. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Repeat the film after removing external lines from the field if position remains unclear.
- Have the cardiac device lead tips moved? (Read A) | Reason: Different projection, position and inspiration change the projected position of the leads over the heart. | Recommend: Review in PACS against the prior. If displacement is a clinical concern, obtain PA and lateral films when the patient is able and a device check.
- Is there a small pneumothorax? (Reads A and B) | Reason: A supine film is insensitive, because air collects anteriorly and at the bases. No pleural line is seen, but that does not exclude it. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest if clinically suspected.
- Is the upper mediastinum truly wider than before? (Read A) | Reason: AP supine projection and rotation widen the mediastinal shadow compared with the PA upright prior. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA when the patient is able, or CT chest if clinically indicated.
- Are there small lung nodules on either study? (Read A) | Reason: The portable film has low contrast and diffuse opacities. The device generator and external hardware obscure parts of both lungs. Small nodules are not reliably seen on X-ray. | Recommend: CT chest if clinically relevant.
- Are there pleural effusions, and are they new? (Read B) | Reason: On a supine film fluid layers posteriorly and shows only as a hazy veil. The lower zones are also crowded by low volumes. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is there a left pleural effusion or retrocardiac collapse or consolidation? (Read B) | Reason: The left base is hidden behind the heart on a low-volume supine AP film. The left costophrenic angle was already slightly hazy on the prior. | Recommend: Upright PA and lateral when the patient is able, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is the basal opacity true new airspace disease or an effect of technique? (Read B) | Reason: Low inspiration and supine position crowd the lower zones and mimic basal opacity. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration, upright if possible, or CT chest.
- Is an endotracheal tube present, and where is its tip relative to the carina? Is an enteric tube present, and where does it end? (Read B) | Reason: The tube outline and carina are not clearly resolved on this compressed image, and overlying leads and wires confuse the midline. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing and confirm tube positions clinically. Repeat the film if the tip is not seen.
- Is the mediastinum widened? (Read B) | Reason: Supine AP projection with mild rotation and low volumes widens the mediastinal shadow. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.

IMPRESSION:
1. Tubular density over the trachea consistent with an endotracheal tube, tip over the upper thoracic trachea, not on the prior. Indeterminate: the reads disagreed on status, and the carina is not clearly defined, so tip-to-carina position is unconfirmed. Confirm on the source image and clinically. The indication does not mention intubation. Triage flagged critical with on-call page.
2. Increased coarse reticular and hazy opacity in the right mid zone, with supine AP technique contributing.
3. Increased coarse reticular and hazy opacity in the left mid zone, similar in pattern. Together with item 2, the pattern is consistent with interstitial fluid or another diffuse process. Infection or another diffuse process is not excluded on a supine, low-volume film.
4. Hazy right lower zone opacity, indeterminate (atelectasis, airspace opacity or layering fluid; both reads indeterminate).
5. Hazy left base and retrocardiac opacity with poorly defined left hemidiaphragm, indeterminate (both reads indeterminate).
6. Left pectoral cardiac device with the same lead configuration as the prior. Indeterminate: the reads disagreed on status, and lead tip movement cannot be judged given the projection change. No lead discontinuity is seen at this resolution.
7. Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both films. Interval change in size cannot be determined (AP supine versus PA).
8. Apparent upper mediastinal widening is indeterminate (one read only; AP supine projection and rotation).
9. Pleural effusion, pneumothorax and free gas are undetermined on this supine film. No discrete lung mass or definite focal bone lesion is seen at this resolution.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review the source image in PACS with windowing now to confirm endotracheal tube tip relative to the carina and the presence and position of any enteric tube. Repeat chest radiograph with external lines out of the field if position remains unclear.
- Repeat chest radiograph, upright PA and lateral, when the patient is able, to reassess heart size, mediastinal width, effusion and basal opacities.
- Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest if effusion, pneumothorax or basal consolidation needs to be settled clinically.
- Cardiac device check if lead displacement is a clinical concern.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
